issues.description: The UML in the problem statement declares Animal(String, int) (an Animal constructor taking name and age), but the provided solution and the template Main use single-argument constructors for animals (e.g., new Seal("Clarabelle")). This constructor parameter mismatch will confuse students about which constructor signature to implement and can cause tests or template usage to fail if they follow the UML instead of the template usage.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor signature consistent across artifacts. Either update the UML/problem statement to require Animal(String) (remove age) and document that only name is required, or update the template and solution so all Animal subclasses and their usages accept (String, int) and include the age attribute. Also update Main and example usages to match the chosen constructor signature.

issues.description: The UML and diagram list an age attribute for Animal (age: int), but the textual description emphasizes only name and the solution's Animal implementation lacks the age attribute entirely. This attribute mismatch between the UML and the implemented/template code is ambiguous and may lead students to implement an unexpected field or miss required getters/setters.
issues.suggestedFix: Clarify the intended attributes for Animal in the problem statement. Either remove the age attribute from the UML and description so that only name is required, or add age to the template and solution (including constructor, field, and getter/setter) and update example usages to pass an age value.

issues.description: The problem UML and description specify Animal has two attributes (name and age) and a constructor Animal(String, int), but the provided solution's Animal class only defines a single 'name' attribute and a constructor Animal(String). This mismatch between the problem statement (and UML) and the solution/template creates a conceptual mapping gap: students expecting to implement or use Animal(String, int) and an 'age' field will find the reference solution uses a different constructor and lacks the 'age' identifier.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the implementation with the UML: add a private int age field to Animal, change the constructor to public Animal(String name, int age), and provide corresponding getAge()/setAge(int) methods. Update subclasses' constructors to call super(name, age) and adjust example/main usage accordingly so the identifier and signature match the problem description.
